body_markdown:
Bolt.new has gained significant traction as a browser-based AI app builder, reaching an estimated $40M in annual recurring revenue by March 2025 after its October 2024 launch. However, teams seeking a different development workflow, integrated backend infrastructure, or more flexible mobile app publishing may find that other platforms better suit their needs. This guide compares seven Bolt.new alternatives, including[Floot](https://floot.com/) , for building and publishing AI-powered applications.


For teams already using Claude or ChatGPT, Floot offers a different approach. It is a full-stack app-building platform whose[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) connects supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, to managed infrastructure. The connected AI assistant handles development, while Floot provides the services needed to run and publish applications. Available building capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **MCP connector architecture changes cost structure** : Floot lets users build through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, using its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) and their existing AI subscriptions instead of paying separate Floot AI build-credit charges for connector-based code generation.
- **Mobile app publishing is available across plans** : Floot packages web apps into[iOS and Android applications](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) , with 2 monthly mobile builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Connected developer accounts enable TestFlight uploads on all plans, while Google Play publishing requires Pro or Power.
- **Managed infrastructure supports full-stack applications** : Floot provides[built-in infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including managed Postgres databases, authentication, backend endpoints, file storage, hosting, and transactional email. Payments are available for testing on Free and live transactions on eligible paid plans.
- **Pricing separates building from application usage** : Floot measures connector work through build actions, with 100 daily actions on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power. Hosting usage and optional AI features have separate allowances and charges.
- **Existing AI tools support familiar workflows** : Floot's MCP integration lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, reducing the need to switch between development environments.


## **Understanding Bolt.new and Why Teams Seek Alternatives**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI app builder from StackBlitz that generates full-stack applications from natural language prompts. The platform provides an in-browser development environment with Bolt Cloud for database, authentication, and hosting services. It supports Figma and screenshot imports for design-to-code workflows and offers bidirectional GitHub synchronization for developer-centric teams.


Common reasons teams explore Bolt.new alternatives include:


- **Token consumption concerns** : Complex builds or debugging loops can consume monthly token allowances quickly.
- **Existing AI subscriptions** : Teams already paying for ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro may prefer platforms that leverage those subscriptions.
- **Mobile app requirements** : Different workflows for building and publishing iOS and Android apps.
- **Backend integration preferences** : Some teams want databases, authentication, and hosting included without external service setup.
- **Workflow integration** : Builders who prefer working within their existing AI assistant rather than switching to a separate platform.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants. Its[MCP integration](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides the managed infrastructure, while the connected AI assistant handles development within the permissions available to that client.


### **Key Capabilities for App Building**


- **MCP connector for AI assistants** : Connect Floot to Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, or other compatible MCP clients to build and refine applications through natural language.
- **Complete managed infrastructure** : Every Floot project includes managed Postgres databases, serverless backend endpoints, user authentication, file storage with CDN delivery, and transactional email. Sending emails to external recipients requires a verified sending domain, available on paid plans.
- **Native mobile app builds** : Floot packages web apps into installable iOS and Android shells. It can upload builds to TestFlight and Google Play internal testing tracks through connected developer accounts without requiring a Mac or Xcode.
- **Built-in SEO controls** : Optional server-side pre-rendering lets crawlers receive page-specific HTML, titles, and descriptions. Floot also provides sitemap, metadata, and canonical URL capabilities through its[SEO tools](https://floot.com/en/seo) .
- **Code editor integration** : Connect Floot with Cursor, VS Code, Zed, or other supported clients through its remote MCP server. The[MCP client documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/other-mcp-clients) explains supported connection methods.
- **Integrated payment workflows** : Floot supports Stripe payments, including checkout and subscription workflows. Users can test payments on the Free plan, while live payments require Pro or Power and a connected Stripe account.


### **Build Workflow and Experience**


Floot's approach centers on conversational development. Describe an app in a supported AI assistant, such as "Build a bakery website with a menu page, photo gallery, and contact form," and the assistant can use Floot's connector to create project files, configure the database, and generate a live preview. Refinements happen through continued conversation, subject to the AI client's connector permissions. Published apps can use yourname.floot.app subdomains, while[custom domains](https://floot.com/en/pricing) are available on paid plans.


The platform's[Examples mode](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/examples) lets teams create and inspect edge-case states such as oversized uploads, loading screens, empty views, and small-screen layouts, helping catch issues before users encounter them.


### **Pricing Structure**


Floot is free to start, with paid plans for higher building allowances and additional capabilities. The following prices reflect the listed monthly rates on[Floot's pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) as of October 2026.


- **Free ($0/month)** : 100 build actions per day, a one-time $3 starter hosting allowance, 3,000 starter AI credits, and 2 mobile app builds per month. Build actions reset daily, with no weekly cap.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds per month, and custom domains, including one free domain for eligible users.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 daily build actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25/month hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds.


Annual billing provides two months free. Users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database export is available across plans, while full-project ZIP downloads require a paid plan.


Connector-based development uses the connected AI assistant's own subscription and Floot's build-action allowance. Floot AI credits apply to features such as image generation, AI inside published applications, and the optional Floot AI agent. Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-based and draws from prepaid credits.


Live payments through Floot's integrated Stripe workflow are available on Pro and Power. Pro carries a 1% Floot platform fee per payment, while Power has no Floot platform fee. Stripe processing fees still apply.


### **Why Floot Stands Out**


Floot's MCP connector architecture provides a practical alternative to paying separately for another AI coding interface. When building through supported Claude or ChatGPT configurations, the AI work uses the existing subscription rather than consuming Floot AI build credits. Floot meters connector actions and hosting separately, while optional AI features use their own credits.


Its managed infrastructure is another advantage for non-technical founders and operators. Databases, authentication, hosting, storage, and email are integrated into the app-building environment, reducing the need to configure separate services. With[Floot's payment tools](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) , builders can also add checkout or subscription functionality without implementing payment infrastructure from scratch.


The platform has a[4.8/5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/floot/reviews) based on eight user reviews.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable (formerly GPT Engineer) is a standalone AI app builder that generates full-stack applications from prompts.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Prompt-to-app generation** : Describe applications and receive a complete frontend and backend.
- **Managed backend** : Lovable Cloud provides databases and authentication, with Supabase integration also available.
- **Figma import** : Convert designs directly into functional applications.
- **GitHub synchronization** : Sync projects with GitHub repositories.
- **Large community** : 160,000+ Discord members for support and templates.


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable uses its own AI agent for code generation, with usage measured in credits. The platform supports full-stack application development through Lovable Cloud, with Supabase available as an integration option. The platform supports React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS applications with managed backend services. The credit-based model means complex builds or debugging sessions consume credits as the AI iterates on solutions.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable suits teams who prefer a standalone web interface for app building with managed backend services. The platform primarily focuses on web application development.


## **3. Replit**


Replit is an established cloud development platform with over 60 million users, offering Replit Agent for AI-assisted application development alongside its traditional IDE features.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Full IDE environment** : Browser-based development with support for 50+ programming languages.
- **Replit Agent** : AI assistant for building applications through natural language.
- **Built-in hosting** : Deploy applications directly from the platform.
- **Real-time collaboration** : Multiplayer coding features for team development.
- **Database and authentication** : Integrated services for application backends.


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit provides a comprehensive development environment that goes beyond AI app building to include traditional coding workflows, version control, and collaboration tools. The platform suits both learning environments and production application development. It also supports building and deploying Replit apps directly through ChatGPT.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit works well for teams wanting a full IDE experience with AI assistance, developers learning to code, or organizations needing collaborative development environments. Its full IDE and AI-assisted conversational workflows give teams multiple ways to build and maintain applications.


## **4. Base44**


Base44 is an AI-led app-building platform that Wix acquired in June 2025. The platform focuses on generating functional applications from natural language descriptions.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-led workflow** : Describe applications in natural language for automatic generation.
- **Built-in backend** : Includes database and server-side functionality.
- **Visual editing** : Modify generated applications through a visual interface.
- **Wix ownership** : Acquired by Wix in June 2025 while continuing to operate as a distinct app-building product.


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 provides a standalone AI app-building experience with its own interface and AI agent. The platform offers managed backend capabilities alongside natural-language application development.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 suits teams seeking a standalone, conversational AI app builder with managed backend services.


## **5. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is Vercel's AI-powered tool for generating React and Next.js interfaces and full-stack applications, including backend functionality through supported integrations.


### **Primary Focus**


- **UI component generation** : Creates React components and interfaces from descriptions.
- **Next.js optimization** : Components designed for the Next.js framework.
- **Vercel integration** : Direct deployment to Vercel's hosting platform.
- **Component library** : Browse and customize community-created components.
- **Code export** : Download generated components for use in existing projects.


### **App Building Considerations**


v0 supports full-stack Next.js applications, including backend routes and database-backed features. Persistent data can be added through integrations with providers such as Supabase, Neon, and Upstash. Teams can use v0 to develop complete applications or contribute generated components to existing projects.


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 suits teams already using Next.js and Vercel who want to generate interfaces or full-stack applications. It supports end-to-end app workflows and can also contribute code to existing projects.


## **6. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites is OpenAI's built-in tool for creating, previewing, hosting, and sharing interactive websites and lightweight web apps directly within ChatGPT. Users can describe what they want, refine the result through conversation, and publish it without setting up a separate hosting service.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Conversational website creation** : Build and refine websites and lightweight web apps using ChatGPT prompts.
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish projects to hosted URLs with configurable sharing settings.
- **Interactive functionality** : Create dashboards, forms, and other applications with persistent data.
- **Access controls** : Share privately, within a workspace, or publicly where permitted.
- **Plan-based usage** : Building and editing count toward Codex usage, with hosting and storage subject to applicable limits.


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites offers a built-in publishing workflow for eligible ChatGPT users. It supports databases, file storage, and interactive functionality, although supported features, usage limits, and sharing permissions depend on the plan and workspace.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites suits users who want to create and publish websites or lightweight applications directly within ChatGPT. Floot offers a separate full-stack app-building platform with managed Postgres databases, application authentication, backend endpoints, payment workflows, and mobile app packaging.


## **7. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual app builder combining AI-assisted app generation with a drag-and-drop editing interface. The platform has served the no-code market for years with comprehensive workflow tooling.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual drag-and-drop builder** : Construct applications through a graphical interface.
- **AI-assisted generation** : AI Agent helps generate applications from natural language.
- **Workflow automation** : Build complex logic without writing code.
- **Plugin marketplace** : Extend functionality through community plugins.
- **Built-in database** : Store and manage application data.


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble combines natural-language prompting through its AI Agent with visual editing of interfaces, databases, and workflows. Applications remain within Bubble's ecosystem, combining AI-assisted generation with visual drag-and-drop editing and proprietary workflow logic.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble suits teams interested in combining AI-assisted generation with visual programming. The learning curve for Bubble's specific approach differs from conversational AI builders.


## **Why Floot Stands Out as the Top Bolt.new Alternative**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) brings full-stack app building into the AI assistants teams already use. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations to create, edit, test, and publish applications, depending on connector permissions. Floot provides[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, hosting, backend endpoints, and transactional email.


Connector-based development uses existing AI subscriptions without requiring a second AI model payment to Floot. Its[plans and allowances](https://floot.com/en/pricing) cover daily building actions, hosting, and optional AI credits. Floot also supports[payment integrations](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) , with test checkouts on Free and live transactions on paid plans.


Teams can create[iOS and Android apps](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) and upload builds to app-store testing tracks while retaining control of developer accounts and final submissions. Floot suits founders, operators, and teams building applications with user accounts, saved data, and business logic without manually configuring backend infrastructure.


Floot also supports AI-powered functionality inside published apps, including text generation, image generation, embeddings, and speech-to-text. These features can use Floot's managed AI service, with usage charged against Floot AI credits, or a connected AI provider's API key.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main difference between Floot and Bolt.new?**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector for supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. It uses the connected assistant for development and Floot for managed infrastructure. Bolt.new is a standalone browser-based platform with its own AI agent and token-based usage model. For users already paying for Claude or ChatGPT, Floot's connector-based development avoids a second Floot AI build-credit charge. Floot provides managed Postgres databases, authentication, hosting, and email, while Bolt.new offers managed backend capabilities through Bolt Cloud and supported external integrations.


### **How does Floot's pricing compare to Bolt.new for active builders?**


Bolt.new Pro starts at $25/month with 10 million tokens per month. Floot Pro also costs $25/month, but its pricing page lists a different set of allowances: 1,000 build actions per day, 5,000 monthly AI credits for eligible features, a $10/month hosting allowance, and 12 mobile builds per month. Floot also offers a Free plan with 100 daily actions and a Power plan with 5,000 daily actions. Floot's[build-action limits](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-actions) reset daily, with no weekly cap on any plan. For teams already paying for Claude or ChatGPT, connector-based code generation uses the existing AI subscription. Floot plan fees, hosting overages, and optional AI features remain separate costs.


### **Can mobile apps be built with Floot, and what are the requirements?**


Yes. Floot packages web apps into installable native shells for iOS and Android. Floot handles the cloud-based builds without requiring a Mac, Xcode, or Android Studio. Free plans include 2 mobile builds per month, Pro includes 12, and Power provides unlimited builds. To publish through the stores, an Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year) or Google Play developer account ($25 one-time) is required, depending on the target platform. Google Play connections require a paid Floot plan. Floot can upload builds to TestFlight and Google Play internal testing tracks, but users remain responsible for final store submissions. Apple and Google determine whether submitted apps are approved. The[mobile publishing guide](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) explains account connections and testing workflows.


### **What backend services does Floot provide compared to alternatives?**


Floot includes[managed Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , serverless backend endpoints, user authentication, file storage with CDN delivery, and transactional email. Authentication supports email and password alongside configurable social sign-in options. Database export is available on every plan, while[seven-day database recovery](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) history is a paid-plan feature. Floot also supports Stripe payments, with test transactions available on Free and live payment processing requiring Pro or Power. These services help non-technical builders create applications with saved data, accounts, and backend functionality without manually configuring separate infrastructure providers.


### **How does Floot compare to visual builders like Bubble?**


Floot and Bubble represent different approaches to no-code development. Floot uses conversational AI through supported assistants to generate and maintain TypeScript and React applications, while Bubble combines AI-assisted generation with visual drag-and-drop editing and proprietary workflow logic. Bubble also supports MCP connections to external AI assistants, but its applications remain within Bubble's visual development environment. Floot suits teams that prefer natural-language interaction and want standard code output. Users own their code and data on every plan, while full-project ZIP downloads are available on paid plans through Floot's[code export tools](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) . Bubble suits teams interested in combining AI-assisted generation with visual programming. Both platforms provide hosting and database capabilities.
